_what: NEW source terms that Medi Lexi does not have at all -- the coverage gap of COMPANION_PLAN section 20: electrolytes and common labs, vitals, dosing vocabulary (dose, route, frequency, units), the most-prescribed drug classes, plain-speech body parts, and the ordinary verbs of clinical instruction. Roughly 500-800 of the highest-frequency spoken clinical terms.
_gate: TWO steps, not four (section 21c). 1) Propose the term list plus target pairs, with register and field tags. 2) Native review of the PAIR ONLY -- is this what a practitioner says? Check a reference where one exists; FLAG AND OMIT where none does. Dropped: definitions in any language, word parts, level grading, register curation. Kept: correctness, and omit-rather-than-guess.
_shape: { "s": "Diuretic", "aka": ["water pill"], "cand": [ { "t": "이뇨제", "reg": "clinical" } ] }  --  `reg` is clinical | lay | regional | abbreviation. Vote counts are never authored; the compiler writes zeros. NO `f` on native terms going forward (section 9b-3, 2026-08-08); batch 1 below carries it as the transition (see _status).
_collision: A term whose slug already exists in src/data MERGES into that entry as an extra candidate rather than replacing it or duplicating the id (section 21d: disagreement is a signal, never a silent overwrite). The compiler enforces this; you do not need to check by hand.
_status: Batch 1 (the measured misses), 2026-08-08, data lane: 16 new terms, KO only. Carries `f` as the deliberate transition -- the compiler still emits it unconditionally, so batch 1 shipped WITH `f` and batch 2 drops it once the coder guards the compiler (section 9b-3).
